solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tree belonging to Henry in country where 17 landed

parts.note: the bay is a laurel tree
of expresses possession, as in 'the house of my father'

indicators.note: the letter for Henry is placed inside the country's name

parts.note: Wales is a country of the United Kingdom
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A tree owned by a man called Henry, in the land where some figure came ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is AMUNDSEN, the Norwegian polar explorer, whose 1911 expedition set up base on the Ross Ice Shelf at this inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: This Antarctic inlet in the Ross Ice Shelf was where Amundsen's party came ashore and set up camp.

clue.text: Poor beaded covering for stone furniture item

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the abbreviation for stone, covering it
poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters of beaded are knocked into a new order

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: Shabby bead-work as a cover for a stone piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' makes BEDEAD, which 'covering' splits to hold the stone abbreviation; 'stone' looks like a material but is the British weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedstead is the frame of a bed, a standard piece of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: We try to restructure phone company's plants

indicators.note: restructuring rebuilds something in a new shape, so the letters of we try are rearranged

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network; with the 's it gives EES

explanation.surface: A boardroom plan to reorganise the phone company's industrial plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to restructure' turns WE TRY into YEWTR. EE is a UK mobile network, its possessive giving EES.
explanation.definitionFit: Yews are evergreen conifers, so several of them are a kind of plant life.

clue.text: Woman has nothing in colour? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside another
the exclamation reverses the stated arrangement, so the colour holds nothing instead of nothing sitting inside the colour

parts.note: FA is short for 'sweet FA', British slang for nothing at all
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A woman wears nothing but a colour, or perhaps it's the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, nothing goes in the colour; 'Quite the opposite!' flips the containment. 'Sweet FA' is British slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Freda is a female first name, so it fits the generic clue word for a lady.

clue.text: Man's Conservative past

parts.note: his is the possessive belonging to a man
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A fellow's past as a Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: One's history is one's record of earlier events, i.e. one's background or former times.

clue.text: Cord some wrapped in fat

indicators.note: one piece is enclosed by another, as a parcel is wrapped in paper

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
any means some, as in 'have you any milk?'

explanation.surface: A length of string coated in grease.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a cord worn round the neck or used on ships for securing things.

clue.text: Where 17 and 25 were headed, only carrying unfashionable sauce

indicators.note: the word for only carries the other pieces inside it

parts.note: sole means only, as in 'the sole survivor'
out means no longer in fashion
HP Sauce is a well-known British brown sauce

explanation.surface: A destination for two numbered figures, involving a dull sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 and 25 are AMUNDSEN and SCOTT, who raced to reach the pole in 1911-12. HP is a British brown sauce brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both explorers aimed for the southernmost point of the Earth in the famous race of 1911-12.

clue.text: Reduces price of lettuce

indicators.note: the word for price is reduced by cutting off its final letter

parts.note: cost means price

explanation.surface: A shop cuts the price of its lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduces price' looks like a definition of discounting; it means COST shortened by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of lettuce with long, crisp leaves, also called romaine.

clue.text: Heartlessly preserving corporal punishment

indicators.note: the heart of the word for preserving, its central letter, is removed

parts.note: canning is preserving food in tins

explanation.surface: Cruelly keeping up beatings as a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' removes one of the two middle Ns of CANNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A beating with a cane was a form of physical punishment once common in schools.

clue.text: Second snake is further down

parts.note: an adder is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A second snake lies lower down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'further down' reads as position but means more depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down means being unhappy, so further down is the comparative form, more unhappy.

clue.text: With some medicine around, try finding water

indicators.note: the dose goes around the letter for with

parts.note: a dose is an amount of medicine

explanation.surface: With medicine on hand, someone goes in search of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowsing is searching for underground water with a divining rod.

clue.text: Study game with coach taking note, reflecting on having been out too long?

indicators.note: reflecting means mirrored, so the whole chain of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: the coach takes the note inside it

parts.note: a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: A student plays, takes a coach and a note, and thinks about having stayed out late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' gives BNUS, and 'reflecting' reverses the whole string DENRUBNUS. 'Out' in the definition means out in the sun, not out on the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying outdoors in strong sun for too long leaves skin red and scorched.

clue.text: Go wrong blocking brown eggs for 25's ship

indicators.note: the word for go wrong sits inside the colour, blocking it

parts.note: tan is a light brown
err means go wrong
ova are eggs

explanation.surface: Something goes awry in a plate of brown eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is SCOTT; his 1910-13 Antarctic expedition sailed in this ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's last Antarctic expedition sailed on this whaler, named after the Latin for Newfoundland.

clue.text: See 15
Cat we saw may lose at first, getting eroded

indicators.note: each of the four words loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cat we spotted might shed something, worn down.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, W, S and M from CAT WE SAW MAY to leave AT E AW AY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ate away means wore down gradually, as water wears rock, a past-tense verb phrase.

clue.text: I'm surprised to receive drivel disguised as comprehensive theory

indicators.note: the exclamation receives the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: wow is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: disguised means changed in appearance, so the letters of drivel are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed to be handed nonsense passed off as a grand theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' gives RLDVIE, which 'to receive' places inside the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A worldview is an all-embracing philosophy or outlook on life.

clue.text: Swinger hero doing wrong

indicators.note: doing something wrong means its letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A dashing playboy who is no hero after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' suggests a socialite but is something that swings.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot fitting lets a door swing open and shut, so it is literally something that swings.

clue.text: Poet loses second fact-checker

indicators.note: the poet loses the letter, which is taken out

parts.note: a versifier is a writer of verse

explanation.surface: A poet loses his job to a fact-checker.
explanation.definitionFit: A verifier confirms that something is true, which is what a fact-checker does.

clue.text: Sun named adventuring explorer

indicators.note: adventuring means roaming about, so the letters of sun named wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper names an explorer out on an adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Amundsen was the Norwegian who led the first party to reach the South Pole in 1911.

clue.text: 17's ship was French-American

explanation.surface: An explorer's vessel was Franco-American.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is AMUNDSEN, whose South Pole expedition sailed in this Norwegian ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Amundsen sailed south in this polar vessel, previously used by Nansen in the Arctic.

clue.text: Old instrument promoted after 1100 makes the 23 of 25's landing

indicators.note: the reversed pieces come after the Roman numeral

parts.note: MC is 1100 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: in a down clue promoted means moved up, so the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: a drum is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: An old instrument is given a boost after a date, making a landing place.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is SOUND and 25 is SCOTT: McMurdo Sound in Antarctica is where Scott's expeditions landed.
explanation.definitionFit: McMurdo Sound is the Antarctic inlet where Scott's expeditions made their base.

clue.text: Possibly Bruce and Ray on the ship's downwind side

parts.note: Bruce Lee the martial artist is one person with that surname
a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: Two men, Bruce and Ray, sit on the sheltered side of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks Bruce as an example of someone called LEE; Ray looks like a name but is a light beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel's lee beam is the direction at right angles to its sheltered side, away from the wind.

clue.text: Stray unfortunately got sold

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wandering animal was sadly sold off.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray is a pet that has wandered off and has no home, such as a missing hound.

clue.text: Shrewd like Old King Cole in the end

parts.note: as means like
Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the ancient Egyptian pharaoh

indicators.note: the end of the word Cole is its last letter

explanation.surface: Clever, like the nursery-rhyme Old King Cole turned out to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old King Cole' reads as one rhyme figure but splits into Old King (TUT) and Cole's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means sharp-witted and quick to spot an advantage.

clue.text: Is sceptical of missing particle searches

indicators.note: the particle goes missing from the word for doubts

parts.note: questions means doubts, is sceptical of
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A scientist doubts whether a missing particle is out there to be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Quests are long expeditions in pursuit of something, i.e. searches.

clue.text: Very German and healthy

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
und is the German word for and

explanation.surface: A German is described as very fit and well.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound means in good condition, as in 'of sound mind and body'.

clue.text: Wrongly catalogue way to get lost, you say?

indicators.note: you say signals the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to miss a sign on the road is a way of losing your way

explanation.surface: A librarian mis-files a book, a sure way to get lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To misassign is to allot or file something in the wrong place, like a mislabelled catalogue entry.

clue.text: Explorer's bed in the way

indicators.note: the bed goes inside the abbreviation for the street

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: An explorer's bed is blocking the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Falcon Scott led the British Antarctic expedition that reached the South Pole in 1912.

clue.text: Break stride and run, being calm

indicators.note: breaking the words up lets their letters be reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A runner breaks stride and keeps running, staying composed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not disturbed or agitated stays still and calm, like undisturbed tea or water.

clue.text: Order computers society doesn't mention

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
IT, information technology, means computers

explanation.surface: An order is placed with a computer society which stays silent about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a verb but is the Order of Merit, OM.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to leave something out, so one who omits a fact fails to bring it up.

clue.text: Occasionally selfish characters

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so every other letter of selfish is taken

explanation.surface: Some characters are selfish now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Efs are the written names of the letter F, so they are characters in the sense of letters.

clue.text: Ingeniously grow our thin fencing material

indicators.note: ingeniously means cleverly worked, so the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A clever gardener grows thin plants, perhaps along a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-worked iron is used for decorative railings and gates, a classic material for fences.
